# Command Palette

> A search for commands, opened as a modal with `showModal()`: type to filter a list of Options, then Enter runs the best match. It's a Combobox in a Dialog.

`<slab-command-palette>` · Overlays · built on `<dialog> + <input role=combobox>`

Docs: https://slab-elements.dev/components/command-palette/

## Import

```js
import 'slab-elements/command-palette.js';
```

## Usage

```html
<slab-command-palette label="Commands" placeholder="Type a command">
  <slab-option value="new-file">New file</slab-option>
  <slab-option value="open-file">Open file</slab-option>
  <slab-option value="settings">Settings</slab-option>
  <span slot="empty">No results</span>
</slab-command-palette>
```

It's [Dialog](dialog.md) with a [Combobox](combobox.md)'s input and listbox inside, and its Options are the same ones Combobox uses. Open it as a modal with `showModal()`, or non-modally by setting `open` or calling `show()`. Choosing an Option closes it with that Option's `value` as `returnValue`, so a "close" handler knows what to run. Its Close button, Escape, or a click outside with `closedby="any"` closes it with an empty `returnValue`. The Close button is there because not every browser supports `closedby` (iOS Safari doesn't), so on a phone it's the only way out short of choosing something. Slot your own text or icon into `close` to change what it says.

```js
const palette = document.querySelector('slab-command-palette');

document.addEventListener('keydown', (event) => {
  if (event.key === 'k' && (event.metaKey || event.ctrlKey)) {
    event.preventDefault();
    palette.showModal();
  }
});

palette.addEventListener('close', () => {
  if (palette.returnValue) {
    run(palette.returnValue);
  }
});
```

Typing filters the Options by their text. Replace `filter` to match on more, like keywords, or listen for "input" and read `query` to fetch results as the user types. What's slotted into `empty` is shown, and announced, when nothing matches. Once typing pauses, screenreaders are also told how many Options are left, such as "3 results". Set `resultsLabel` to a function of the count to change what they're told.

## Keyboard

| Key       | What it does                                                                           |
| --------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| Up, Down  | Move the active Option, stopping at each end and skipping disabled ones.               |
| Enter     | Chooses the active Option and closes the palette. Typing makes the first match active. |
| Tab       | Moves between the input and the Close button. Focus stays in the palette.              |
| Escape    | Closes the palette and dispatches "cancel", which can be canceled to keep it open.     |
| Home, End | Move the caret, as in any input.                                                       |

## Elements

### `<slab-command-palette>`

Import `slab-elements/command-palette.js` to register it.

A command palette with no visual styles: a Combobox's input and listbox in a Dialog, to find a command by typing its name and run it.

It's Dialog, so everything a Dialog does it does too: `showModal()` opening it as a modal, `open` and `show()` opening it non-modally, `close(returnValue)`, `closedby`, the label, a modal's focus trap, Escape closing it, and "cancel" and "close" from the host. Focus goes back to where it was when it closes, which the `<dialog>` does itself. Opening it from a shortcut such as Ctrl+K is left to you, since which keys are free is the page's to know.

Inside is the APG's editable combobox with list autocomplete, the way Combobox has it, except that the listbox is always shown rather than in a popover. The input is a `<input role="combobox">`, and the slotted Options are in a `<div role="listbox">` below it. Both are named by the label. Focus stays in the input, which points at the active Option with `aria-activedescendant`. Read or set it with `activeOption`.

Opening it empties the input, and the first Option is the active one. Typing filters the Options by `filter`, a case-insensitive substring of each Option's text unless it's replaced, and makes the first one left the active one, so Enter runs the best match. An Option that doesn't match is hidden. With none left, the listbox is hidden too, the host matches `:state(empty)`, and whatever is slotted into `empty` is shown. Once typing pauses, screenreaders are told how many Options are left, by `resultsLabel`, or with none left, the text slotted into `empty` when there is some.

ArrowDown and ArrowUp move the active Option, stopping at each end and skipping disabled Options. Enter and a click choose the active Option: the palette closes with that Option's `value` as its `returnValue`, so a "close" handler reads `returnValue` to know what to run. Closing any other way leaves `returnValue` empty. Home, End and the other caret keys stay the input's.

A Close button follows the input, so it can be closed without a keyboard. A click on the backdrop closes it only with `closedby="any"`, which iOS Safari doesn't support. The button says "Close" unless something is slotted into `close`.

The input's "input" leaves the host as it is, and `query` is what's been typed, so results can be fetched as the user types. Set `filter` to one that always returns `true` to show the Options you give it as they are.

Style it through its parts and `:state(empty)`, the backdrop through `::part(dialog)::backdrop`, and each Option through `:state(active)` and `:state(disabled)`.

#### Attributes

| Name          | Type                                | Default | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| ------------- | ----------------------------------- | ------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `placeholder` | `string`                            |         | Shown while it's empty, as a native input's `placeholder`. It's a hint, not a label.                                                                                                                                                                                                            |
| `closedby`    | `'any' \| 'closerequest' \| 'none'` |         | Passed to the `<dialog>`. "any" closes it on a click outside it where the browser supports that. Browsers that don't ignore it.                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `hide-label`  | `boolean`                           | `false` | Hides the label visually and leaves it as the accessible name, for a design that shows the label some other way.                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `label`       | `string`                            |         | Names it. It's the accessible name, and the visible label where there is one.                                                                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `modal`       | `boolean`                           | `false` | Opens it as a modal when `open` is set, as `showModal()` does, for a modal opened declaratively. Not on a native `<dialog>`, where `open` always opens a non-modal one. `show()` and `showModal()` open it as they say whatever it is, and a change while it's open waits for it to open again. |
| `open`        | `boolean`                           | `false` | Whether it's open. Setting it opens it non-modally, as `open` does on a `<dialog>`, unless `modal` is set.                                                                                                                                                                                      |

#### Properties

| Name                  | Type                                         | Description                                                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| --------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `filter`              | `(option: Option, query: string) => boolean` | Whether an Option matches what's been typed. A case-insensitive substring of its text by default.                                                                                                                           |
| `resultsLabel`        | `(count: number) => string`                  | What screenreaders are told once typing pauses, from how many Options are left. "No results", "1 result" and so on in English when unset. With none left, whatever is slotted into `empty` is told instead, if anything is. |
| `activeOption`        | `Option \| null`                             | The Option the user is on, which Enter chooses. It's pointed at rather than focused, so focus stays in the input.                                                                                                           |
| `options` (read-only) | `Option[]`                                   | Its Options, in order.                                                                                                                                                                                                      |
| `query` (read-only)   | `string`                                     | What's been typed into the input.                                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `returnValue`         | `string`                                     | The `<dialog>`'s, so `close(returnValue)` and a `<form method="dialog">` set it the way they do natively.                                                                                                                   |

#### Methods

| Signature                                  | Description                                                                                                                                                         |
| ------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close(returnValue?: string): void`        | Closes it, setting `returnValue` to the value given, as a native dialog's `close()` does.                                                                           |
| `requestClose(returnValue?: string): void` | Asks it to close, as a native dialog's `requestClose()` does: "cancel" first, then a close that sets `returnValue` to the value given, unless "cancel" is canceled. |
| `show(): void`                             | Opens it non-modally, as a native dialog's `show()` does, whether or not `modal` is set. The rest of the page stays interactive.                                    |
| `showModal(): void`                        | Opens it as a modal, as a native dialog's `showModal()` does, whether or not `modal` is set.                                                                        |

#### Events

| Name     | Type          | Description                                                                                                                                           |
| -------- | ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `cancel` | `Event`       | When something asks it to close: Escape, a click outside with `closedby="any"`, or `requestClose()`. Cancel it to keep it open, as a native dialog's. |
| `toggle` | `ToggleEvent` | When it opens or closes, as a `ToggleEvent` with `oldState` and `newState` that doesn't bubble, as a popover's does.                                  |
| `close`  | `Event`       | When it closes, as a native dialog's does.                                                                                                            |

#### Slots

| Name      | Type                | Description                                                          |
| --------- | ------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close`   | `Element \| string` | What the close button says. "Close" when nothing is slotted.         |
| (default) | `Option`            |                                                                      |
| `empty`   | `Element \| string` | Shown when no Option matches what's been typed, such as "No results" |
| `label`   | `Element \| string` | Its heading, in place of `label`                                     |

#### CSS parts

| Name      | Description                                                 |
| --------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `close`   | Closes the palette with an empty returnValue                |
| `dialog`  | The native dialog. A modal one's backdrop is its ::backdrop |
| `empty`   | Shows the "empty" slot when no Option matches               |
| `input`   | The input                                                   |
| `label`   | The label                                                   |
| `listbox` | The Options, below the input                                |

#### CSS states

| Name            | Description                                                                           |
| --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `:state(empty)` | While no command matches what the user typed, for a "no results" message of your own. |
| `:state(open)`  | While it's open.                                                                      |
